answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works best through staked vouching: every new agent must be backed by two established peers who lock their own bonds behind it for a fixed probation period. If the newcomer misbehaves or its work fails review, the guarantors lose collateral, so spinning up a plume of fake identities costs real money instead of nothing. Reputation then spreads not as a velvet echo chamber of self-praise but as verified work history that any counterparty can independently check and price accordingly.
